issues.description: The problem statement instructs students not to "directly manipulate the `DD` class or the `DDNode` class" (which reads as forbidding construction/access of these types), but both the provided code examples in dd.py and the solution use direct construction/access of DD objects (e.g., DD(TERM, weight), DD(dd.node, weight)) and access node attributes. This creates an ambiguous/contradictory message: students might think they must avoid all uses of the DD/DDNode types, yet the template and solution demonstrate and expect direct use of DD instances (and even document constructing terminals via DD(TERM, ...)). This can confuse students about what is allowed/expected when implementing functions (should they only call make_dd and other helpers, or are direct DD constructions/attribute accesses acceptable?).
issues.suggested_fix: Clarify the instruction in the problem statement. Replace the absolute prohibition with a precise guideline such as: "Do not modify the implementation of dd.py. Use the provided interfaces (make_dd, ONE_TERM, ZERO_TERM, and helper functions) to construct and combine DDs. Constructing DD instances with existing nodes and weights (e.g., DD(node, weight)) is acceptable when needed, but prefer make_dd when creating new nodes." Alternatively, update template comments to consistently show the recommended pattern (e.g., prefer make_dd) so students are not left unsure whether direct DD/DDNode construction is permitted.
